title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any Director (executive or otherwise), as defined in the ASX Listing Rules. This is the only tier the Policy substantively restricts.

tiers.name: Associates and related parties
tiers.description: 'Associate' includes a related body corporate and a director or secretary of a related body corporate. 'Related party' includes a spouse or de facto spouse, a parent, son or daughter, and any entity controlled by such persons. The Policy applies equally to dealings by these persons, and to any company, trust or other entity in which a Key Management Person has a relevant interest, as if the Key Management Person had dealt.

windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the next trading day after such release

windows.end_anchor: beginning of trading on the next trading day after the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose 'any other time' as a Prohibited Period, including when considering matters subject to the ASX Listing Rule 3.1A continuous disclosure exceptions; the Board's decision to impose such a period must be kept confidential by Key Management Personnel and not disclosed to any other person.

rules.detail: 'Securities' expressly includes 'any derivatives including but not limited to options', with no venue limitation, and 'dealing' includes granting, accepting or exercising any option or right/obligation to acquire or dispose of securities. Outside a Prohibited Period, a Key Management Person need only give prior written notification to the Company Secretary/Designated Officer and complete the deal within 7 days; there is no discretionary refusal described for this notification. During a Prohibited Period, dealing is banned absent exceptional-circumstances approval under section 7.
rules.evidence: “securities” includes: ... (h) any derivatives including but not limited to options in respect of any of (a) to (f) above.

rules.detail: The table of contents lists section 9 as 'Short selling and Hedging', but the operative text of section 9 as executed contains only a short selling prohibition (9.1); no hedging-specific clause appears anywhere in the document body.

A prepaid forward or similar monetisation is not named. It is an agreement to dispose of securities, or a grant of a right/obligation to dispose of securities, and so is 'dealing' requiring prior written notification outside a Prohibited Period (approval if inside one).
rules.evidence: entering into any agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of any securities of the Company

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling the Company's securities, with no clearance route or carve-out.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from short selling the Company’s securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named but fall within 'any derivatives' in the securities definition, with no venue limitation, so entering one is 'dealing' requiring prior written notification outside a Prohibited Period.

rules.detail: Margin loans are prohibited unless the Designated Officer gives prior written approval, in its absolute discretion; approval may be conditioned on the Company disclosing the loan's existence and terms (such as trigger points or the financier's right to sell unilaterally) to the ASX.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of the Company’s securities, unless they obtain the prior written approval of the Designated Officer (in its absolute discretion).

rules.detail: The ban and approval requirement in section 8 extends beyond margin loans to 'other security arrangement[s]' generally, so granting any security interest over the shares needs the Designated Officer's prior written approval.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of the Company’s securities, unless they obtain the prior written approval of the Designated Officer (in its absolute discretion).

rules.detail: Any secured financing arrangement over the Company's securities (not just a formal margin loan) requires the Designated Officer's prior written approval, which may be conditioned on ASX disclosure of the arrangement's existence and terms.
rules.evidence: Any approval by the Designated Officer may be subject to the condition that the Company be permitted to disclose to the ASX the existence of the margin loan or security arrangement, and where the Company considers appropriate, any relevant terms such as the trigger points or right of the financier to sell unilaterally.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period, short-term dealing ban, or speculative-trading restriction appears anywhere in the Policy.

exemption_authority: The Board may approve updates, amendments and exemptions to this Policy from time to time. Within a Prohibited Period, the Designated Officer may, in its absolute discretion, approve dealing for exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, a court order or enforceable undertaking, or other exceptional circumstances); the decision is final and binding, need not be reasoned, and a refusal must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Table of contents heading '9 Short selling and Hedging' versus the executed section 9, which contains only '9.1 Key Management Personnel are prohibited from short selling the Company’s securities.'
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executed policy appears to have lost its hedging clause when adapted from a template. There is no operative restriction on hedging vested shares, so an OTC collar's economic-hedge character is not independently banned by a hedging-specific rule and falls to be assessed only under the general securities/dealing definition and the section 6 notification regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into a margin loan or other security arrangement in respect of the Company's securities, unless they obtain the prior written approval of the Designated Officer (in its absolute discretion).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that ban only 'margin loans', this reaches any security arrangement over the shares, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not banned outright but is subject to a single discretionary approval gate with no fixed criteria.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval by the Designated Officer may be subject to the condition that the Company be permitted to disclose to the ASX the existence of the margin loan or security arrangement, and where the Company considers appropriate, any relevant terms such as the trigger points or right of the financier to sell unilaterally.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank collar loan approved under section 8 may need to be publicly disclosed, including price triggers or the bank's unilateral sale rights, which affects deal confidentiality and market-signalling risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “securities” includes: ... (h) any derivatives including but not limited to options in respect of any of (a) to (f) above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC-only put and call collar is unambiguously 'securities'/'dealing', subject to the ordinary notification (open period) or Designated Officer approval (Prohibited Period) regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel must, prior to dealing in the Company's securities, provide the Company Secretary on behalf of the Designated Officer written notification ... of their intention to deal
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside a Prohibited Period, entering the collar's option legs requires only prior notice, not discretionary approval, which is comparatively favourable for timing certainty relative to policies requiring consent for every trade.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender or financier exercising their rights under a loan agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank as secured lender needs to enforce and sell the collared shares, that disposal is expressly excluded from the Prohibited Period ban and the general notification requirement, reducing enforcement friction relative to policies that treat a lender's forced sale as a breach.

summary: A funded collar is comparatively achievable under this policy. Kogan's 'securities' definition expressly includes 'any derivatives including but not limited to options' with no venue restriction, so an OTC put and call are squarely 'dealing' by a Key Management Person (a term that already includes all directors); outside a Prohibited Period this needs only prior written notification to the Company Secretary/Designated Officer and completion within 7 days, with no discretionary refusal described. The loan leg is not banned outright: section 8 requires only the Designated Officer's prior written approval (in its absolute discretion) to enter a margin loan or 'other security arrangement', and approval may be conditioned on ASX disclosure of the arrangement's existence and terms such as price triggers or the financier's unilateral sale right. If the bank later needs to enforce and sell the collared shares as secured lender, that disposal is expressly excluded from the Prohibited Period ban. No hedging-specific restriction or short-term/minimum-holding rule exists in the executed text at all. The principal constraints are the discretionary, unappealable approval for the financing arrangement, the three Prohibited Period blackouts, and the possible ASX-disclosure condition on the loan.
